meta.name: Application Shell
meta.description: Persistent authenticated application structure with global navigation, account context, utilities, and a controlled content canvas.

purpose: Provide a predictable authenticated environment that preserves global navigation and user context while giving product screens a consistent content canvas and scroll model.
useWhen: The product contains several authenticated routes.
Users need persistent access to primary product areas.
Tenant, organization, workspace, or account context must remain visible.
Product screens share global utilities and identity controls.
doNotUseWhen: The route is a focused authentication or account-recovery screen.
The product is a single isolated page without persistent navigation.
A public marketing or documentation experience is being created.
The workflow requires a distraction-free full-screen mode and explicitly replaces the shell.

selectionQuestions: Which global product areas require persistent navigation?
Does organization or tenant context affect all route data?
Who owns vertical scrolling: the browser document or the application content canvas?
Which utilities must remain globally available?
Which routes intentionally suppress or replace the application shell?

regions.name: Primary Navigation
regions.role: Provide persistent access to major product areas using user-oriented grouping.
prohibitedComponents: Brand markup inlined outside the isolated Brand/Logo component

sticky.compactBehavior: Transform into an off-canvas navigation drawer.

scroll.notes: Navigation may scroll independently only when its item count exceeds the viewport.

compact.placement: Off-canvas drawer triggered from the global header.
compact.notes: Focus must be trapped while the drawer is open and restored to the trigger on close.

medium.layout: Icon plus accessible tooltip or expandable label pattern.
medium.notes: Current destination must not depend only on color.

wide.notes: The sidebar must not consume the page content scroll.

ultrawide.layout: Grouped icon and label navigation with optional secondary metadata.
ultrawide.notes: Do not widen the navigation merely because more viewport width exists.

rules: Navigation is organized by user tasks and product areas rather than database entities.
The active route is clearly indicated through text, shape, or icon in addition to color.
Navigation labels must support localization expansion.
Destructive or administrative actions do not appear as ordinary primary navigation items.

regions.name: Global Header
regions.role: Provide compact global orientation, navigation trigger, account context, and approved utilities.
prohibitedComponents: Repeated route title when the page header already owns it
Brand markup inlined outside the isolated Brand/Logo component

sticky.compactBehavior: Remain visible with reduced utilities and an overflow menu.

compact.layout: Navigation trigger, compact product identity, context summary, user menu.
compact.notes: Global search may move to a dedicated overlay or route.

medium.layout: Context, compact utilities, and user menu.
medium.notes: Hide low-frequency utility labels before removing their accessible names.

wide.notes: Keep the header compact in operational products.

ultrawide.notes: Do not add decorative empty space.

rules: The global header remains visually subordinate to route content.
Page-specific actions belong to the page recipe unless explicitly global.
Organization or tenant switching must trigger safe context reset and cache isolation.
Icon-only utilities require accessible names.

regions.name: Content Canvas
regions.role: Host route-level screen recipes inside a consistent width, spacing, and scrolling environment.

scroll.notes: The application must use one primary vertical content scroll container.

regions.visibilityCondition: Always visible when the authenticated shell is active.

compact.notes: Page recipes own internal responsive transformation.

medium.placement: Beside the navigation rail and below the header.

wide.placement: Beside the sidebar and below the header.
wide.notes: Screen recipes select constrained, fluid, or hybrid page containers.

ultrawide.placement: Beside the sidebar and below the header.
ultrawide.layout: Fluid content canvas with recipe-controlled maximum widths.
ultrawide.notes: Do not stretch reading or form content indefinitely.

rules: Route screens must expose one route-level heading.
The content canvas does not wrap every route in an additional card.
Screen recipes control page padding and maximum width through approved layout components.
Route errors should remain inside the content canvas unless authentication has failed.

regions.name: Global Feedback Layer
regions.role: Present application-wide overlays, toasts, command interfaces, and session-level feedback.
regions.visibilityCondition: Rendered as infrastructure; visible only when feedback or overlay state is active.

compact.layout: Full-width or near-full-width overlays where appropriate.
compact.notes: Dialogs must respect compact viewport height.

medium.layout: Centered or edge-aligned overlay according to component contract.
medium.notes: Focus management is owned by overlay components.

ultrawide.notes: Overlay width remains constrained by component contracts.

rules: Global toasts do not replace local field or form errors.
Session expiration must preserve safe recovery behavior.
Overlays use semantic z-index tokens.
Global feedback must not expose raw technical errors.

composition.columnPolicy: Persistent navigation plus one flexible content column at medium and wider layouts; single content column with off-canvas navigation at compact width.
spacingOwnership: The shell owns the relationship between navigation, global header, and content canvas.
Individual screen recipes own padding and spacing inside the content canvas.
Global feedback overlays own their internal spacing.
surfacePolicy: Navigation and global header use approved shell surfaces.
The content canvas uses the application canvas token.
Do not add an extra card around every route.
rules: Use one primary vertical content scroll container.
Persistent navigation must not shift route layout unexpectedly.
Shell regions must remain independent of feature-specific data fetching.
Tenant or organization switching must not leave previous-context data visible.
prohibited: Several independent full-height vertical scroll containers.
Page-specific actions placed globally without a product-wide reason.
Absolute positioning used to create the primary shell layout.

actions.primaryPlacement: Owned by the active screen recipe, not the global shell.
actions.secondaryPlacement: Global utilities may appear in the global header when they apply across routes.
actions.destructivePlacement: Never placed as an ordinary global shell action.
actions.contextualPlacement: User menu, organization switcher, and approved global utility menus.
actions.overflowPolicy: Low-frequency global utilities move to an accessible overflow menu before being removed.
actions.compactBehavior: Preserve navigation trigger, active context, and user access; move secondary utilities to overflow.
rules: The shell does not compete visually with the active screen.
Logout remains discoverable but is not styled as the screen's primary action.
Global utilities must have product-wide scope.

content.headingPolicy: The shell does not own the route-level h1; each active screen owns one.
content.longContentPolicy: Navigation labels may wrap only when the approved navigation component supports it; otherwise use concise labels and accessible full names.
content.truncationPolicy: Organization or tenant names may truncate only when the full value remains accessible.
content.emptyStatePlacement: The shell does not render feature empty states; route recipes own them.
content.loadingStrategy: Application bootstrap may show a shell-level loading boundary before authenticated context is available; route loading occurs inside the content canvas.
content.errorScope: Authentication or application-bootstrap failures may replace the content canvas; feature errors remain route-local.
rules: The shell remains visually restrained.
Global context must be understandable without exposing technical identifiers.
Product identity must not consume excessive operational space.

responsive.minimumViewport: 320 CSS pixels with declared workflow limitations where applicable.
responsive.zoomExpectation: The shell must remain navigable at 125% browser zoom.
responsive.internalOverflowPolicy: Navigation may scroll vertically; overlays may scroll internally; the main route owns ordinary content overflow.

transformations.change: Keep the persistent sidebar and remove any nonessential secondary metadata from navigation.
transformations.reason: Preserve content width and reduce navigation visual weight.

transformations.change: Transform the full sidebar into a compact navigation rail and move low-frequency utilities to overflow.
transformations.reason: Preserve useful content width while maintaining persistent route access.

transformations.change: Replace persistent navigation with an off-canvas drawer and simplify the global header.
transformations.reason: A persistent rail would consume excessive compact viewport width.

states.rendering: Show an application bootstrap state until authentication, runtime configuration, and organization context are resolved.
states.userAction: Wait or recover when bootstrap fails.
states.notes: Do not briefly render protected route content before authentication is resolved.

states.rendering: Render the authenticated shell and active route.
Render a safe application-level recovery state for bootstrap failures.
states.userAction: Retry, sign in again, or contact support using a safe correlation identifier.

states.rendering: Redirect to or render the approved authentication recovery flow.
Keep the shell when the user is authenticated but lacks route capability, unless disclosure is unsafe.
states.userAction: Return to an available product area.

states.rendering: Render a controlled service-unavailable state without exposing raw infrastructure details.

landmarkMap: Primary navigation uses a labeled nav landmark.
Global header uses a header landmark.
Active route content uses exactly one main landmark.
Overlay components use their native dialog, menu, or status semantics.
headingStructure: The shell does not create an additional route-level h1.
The active route supplies exactly one h1.
Navigation group labels do not replace route headings.
focusOrder: Primary navigation or compact navigation trigger.
keyboard: Provide a skip link to the main route content.
Off-canvas navigation traps focus while open and restores focus on close.
User and organization menus follow approved menu keyboard behavior.
announcements: Route changes should update the document title and provide route orientation where required.
Session expiration and context changes must be perceivable.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Active navigation, selected context, and system states must not depend only on color.
rules: Do not create duplicate unlabeled navigation landmarks.
Hidden compact navigation must not remain focusable.
Persistent shell controls require visible focus.

prohibitedPatterns: Global page actions duplicated inside the shell.
Navigation organized directly from backend modules.
Raw tenant or account identifiers shown as ordinary labels.
dataMagnitude: Navigation must support several grouped product areas without requiring every route to remain simultaneously visible.
Organization names may be significantly longer than fixture examples.
performance: The shell should not rerender all route content for unrelated navigation-state changes.
Large route modules may use route-level lazy loading.
Global providers should remain minimal and stable.
implementation: Use approved navigation and overlay primitives.
Centralize route definitions and active-state calculation.
Do not access authentication tokens directly inside shell presentation components.
Machine presence conditions come from presenceDefaults; visibilityCondition prose is explanatory only.

presenceDefaults.rationale: The authenticated application shell always provides primary product navigation; compact layouts transform its presentation rather than removing the region.
The shell always provides global orientation and account/context utilities while the shell is active.
The shell is incomplete without the route content canvas that owns the active product screen.
Global feedback is structural portal infrastructure that remains mounted; individual toasts, dialogs, and command surfaces control their own visible state.

checks.description: The application-shell recipe must validate against the layout recipe schema.
checks.remediation: Correct missing or invalid recipe fields.

checks.description: The shell must not introduce page-level horizontal overflow at approved viewports and 125% zoom.
checks.remediation: Correct navigation width, content sizing, or compact transformation.

checks.description: Compact navigation must trap and restore focus correctly.
checks.remediation: Use the approved drawer primitive and correct focus lifecycle.

checks.description: The authenticated shell must not expose content from the previous tenant or organization after context switching.
checks.remediation: Correct query-cache isolation and context bootstrap behavior.

checks.description: The shell should remain visually subordinate to route-level tasks.
checks.remediation: Reduce shell height, decoration, or redundant content.

checks.description: Application-shell geometry and structural presence must come from typed recipe defaults; global feedback remains mounted infrastructure even when no overlay is visible.
checks.remediation: Correct craftDefaults/presenceDefaults and keep conditional regions required=false with cardinality.minimum=0.

examples.name: Authenticated operational application
examples.description: Persistent sidebar, compact global header, fluid route content, and portal-based feedback layer.
